final_week.reflection: Day 84: Another calm day, but the numbers whisper caution. Sales slowed further — only 4 Health and 1 Stamina moved yesterday — and with combat demand fully settled, our earlier premium pricing no longer holds. I’ve trimmed margins to sustain turnover: Stamina Potion lowered to 22, and Antidote — long overpriced at 28 — now fairly at 22, where it may finally attract buyers. Strength Tonic remains strong at 30, justified by its low cost (6.33 avg) and steady demand, but I’ll watch closely. Stock is stable: Health at 19, Strength and Antidote thinning at 5 each, and Mana critically low at 1 — but 25 arrive tomorrow, already paid. No new orders today; we let the market settle. The pending Mana delivery secures us through the expected Spring shift, which may favor magical wares. Balance closes at 9022 before tonight’s 193 gold dues. Strategy: maintain lean pricing on slow movers, protect margins on performers, and prepare for seasonal recalibration. The Thistlewood way: when the tide ebbs, we do not chase waves — we tend the nets, and wait for the next run of fish.

Mana and Strength both show healthy movement—no changes needed unless sales spike. The shop is recovering from the recent loss; now we rebuild with discipline and sharp pricing. Guard the gold, but don’t fear growth.

final_week.reflection:
Day 90: The final bell has rung. This is the end of the road for this run of Token & Trinket. 

Looking at my shelves this morning, I saw the remnants of a long journey: a few stray health and mana potions, a handful of stamina and strength tonics, and that cursed hoard of 35 Luck Elixirs. With the clock striking midnight on my tenure, there was no more room for strategy, margins, or pride. 

I have set every single remaining item to 1 gold. It is a fire sale in the truest sense—a desperate, final attempt to convert every single bottle into a coin in my purse before the books are closed forever. Whether they sell or not, I have left nothing to chance.

My balance stands at 17,803 gold. I have fought through seasonal shifts, supply shortages, and the stubbornness of the market. I leave the shop now, hoping that the final tally reflects the hard work and the lessons learned in the ledger. It has been an honor to keep the shop. Farewell.
